source: Thank you for the @g$TotalPrice$. Meet me at the market and I will give you the goods.
text: 谢谢你支付@g$TotalPrice$。到市场来找我，我会把货物交给你。

source: I have just heard that an English ship full of settlers has sunk.
text: 我刚听说，一艘载满移民的英格兰船沉没了。

source: I have just heard that a French ship full of settlers has sunk.
text: 我刚听说，一艘载满移民的法国船沉没了。

source: I have just heard that a Dutch ship full of settlers has sunk.
text: 我刚听说，一艘载满移民的荷兰船沉没了。

source: I have just heard that a Spanish ship full of settlers has sunk.
text: 我刚听说，一艘满载移民的西班牙船沉没了。

source: Unfortunately you do not have enough credit to provide me with a loan.
text: 可惜你的资金不足，无法借款给我。

source: You have also learned something very interesting: the treasure fleet is currently in %1!
text: 你还得知了一条重要消息：宝船队目前就在%1！

source: There is a ship available in the harbor.
text: 港口里有一艘可用的船。

source: A plague has broken out in %1. The quality of life has worsened and the demand for garments and wood is twice as high for one month. While the plague lasts, the town's citizens perish daily and traders are reluctant to sail to the town.
text: %1爆发了瘟疫。生活水平下降，未来一个月内，服装和木材的需求量翻倍。瘟疫期间每天都有居民死去，商人也不愿驶往这座城镇。

source: If you want as many traders as possible to visit your town, you should simply not supply your town with certain goods. You should ideally choose goods that are produced in nearby towns, because traders will take the length of the journey involved into consideration.<n><n>Traders who visit your town automatically buy goods that are in abundance and therefore have low prices in your town. You can sell the goods you have produced to your town directly. As long as the goods are not more expensive than in other towns, they will be purchased regularly by traders.<n><n>The advantage of this is that there are always enough goods available for your citizens and you also don't have to worry about transporting the goods to other towns.
text: 如果希望尽可能多的商人来访，可以有意停止向城镇供应某些商品。最好选择附近城镇生产的商品，因为商人也会考虑航程长短。<n><n>来访商人会自动买入你城里供应过剩、价格低廉的货物。你可以直接把自产商品卖给本城，只要价格不高于其他城镇，商人就会定期来采购。<n><n>这样既能让居民始终得到充足供应，你也不必操心把货物运往其他城镇。

source: Hunt down and kill the bounty hunter staying near the town of @T$Town$ by @D$EndDate$.
text: 在@D$EndDate$前，追踪并杀死逗留在@T$Town$附近的赏金猎人。

source: There you are again, and I see you’ve succeeded.<n><n>So I must keep to my side of our agreement. You will find Master @N$TeacherName$ in his hideout.<n><n> @l$TeacherPos$<n><n>Look along the coast there and you’ll find him.<n><n>Bring @a$Amount$ of wine with you as payment.
text: 你回来了，看样子已经成功。<n><n>那我也该履行约定。你可以在隐居处找到@N$TeacherName$大师。<n><n>@l$TeacherPos$<n><n>沿着那里的海岸找，就能找到他。<n><n>带上@a$Amount$葡萄酒作为酬劳。

source: Thank you for doing me this favor.<n><n>Now to our agreement. The old captain is called @N$TeacherName$ and he has retired not far from here.<n><n>@l$TeacherPos$<n><n>Look along the coast there and you will find him.<n><n>Bring @a$Amount$ of rum with you or he won’t be willing to help.
text: 谢谢你帮我这个忙。<n><n>现在说说我们的约定。那位老船长名叫@N$TeacherName$，退休后住在离这里不远的地方。<n><n>@l$TeacherPos$<n><n>沿着那里的海岸寻找，就能找到他。<n><n>记得带上@a$Amount$朗姆酒，否则他可不愿帮忙。

source: You have done what I asked and I am very grateful to you.<n><n>You will find the teacher named @N$TeacherName$ by the coast.<n><n> @l$TeacherPos$ <n><n>Search the area there and bring @a$Amount$ of food with you, so that he will be willing to help you.
text: 你完成了我的要求，我非常感激。<n><n>你会在海岸边找到名叫@N$TeacherName$的导师。<n><n>@l$TeacherPos$<n><n>搜索那片地区，带上@a$Amount$食物，他才愿意帮助你。

source: <n><n>And send a captain who has no trading experience.
text: <n><n>还有，派一位没有贸易经验的船长来。

source: <n><n>I advise you to send a captain who has no battle experience.
text: <n><n>我建议你派一位没有战斗经验的船长前去。

source: <n><n>Remember to send a captain who has no experience of navigation.
text: <n><n>记得派一位没有航海经验的船长前去。

source: The convoy cannot set sail because the crew's morale is too low. Give them more shore leave or have the convoy blessed in the church.
text: 船队无法出航，因为船员士气太低。请让他们多上岸休息一会儿，或到教堂为船队祈福。

source: We are also at war with %1.
I am therefore assigning you the mission of capturing a colonial town belonging to %2 by %1.    The town must not be the seat of a governor or the viceroy!
text: 因此，我命你在%1前夺取一座属于%2的殖民地城镇。该城镇不能是总督或殖民地总督的驻地！

source: I am therefore assigning you the mission of capturing a colonial town belonging to %2 by %1.    The town must not be the seat of a governor or the viceroy!<n><n>To avoid problems with the other nations, I will issue you with a Letter of Marque against %2.
text: 因此，我命令你在%1之前占领一座属于%2的殖民城镇。这座城镇不能是总督或殖民地总督的驻地！<n><n>为了避免引起其他国家的不满，我会向你签发一张针对%2的私掠许可证。

source: Right-click on convoy to add ships
text: 右键点击船队以加入船只

source: So be it.<n>Your mission is to capture any town belonging to  %2 by %1.
text: 就这么办。<n>你的任务是在%1前夺取任意一座属于%2的城镇。

source: Your mission is to capture any town belonging to %2 by %1.<n>To avoid any problems with the other nations, I will issue you with a Letter of Marque against %2.
text: 你的任务是在%1之前占领任意一座属于%2的城镇。<n>为了避免引起其他国家的不满，我会向你签发一张针对%2的私掠许可证。

source: <n><n>You have now completed all of the scenario objectives.<n><n>You have another 20 days to accumulate further assets before this scenario ends and your score is displayed.<n><n>Note: All of the events that occurred in this scenario may also occur in free-play mode. When wars are being fought, the nations sometimes dispatch buccaneers to sabotage the towns of hostile nations.
text: <n><n>你已完成本关的全部目标。<n><n>你还有20天时间继续积累资产，之后本关结束，并显示最终得分。<n><n>注意：本关发生的所有事件，也可能出现在自由游戏模式中。战争期间，各国有时会派遣私掠者破坏敌国城镇。

source: On behalf of my nation, I would like to thank you for destroying a convoy of the notorious pirate %1.<n><n>You will receive a total reward of %2 for all of the pirate ships you defeated, and I can assure you that my nation is very grateful to you.
text: 你消灭了臭名昭著的海盗%1的一支船队，我谨代表我国向你致谢。<n><n>根据你击败的全部海盗船，你将获得共计%2的赏金。我可以向你保证，我国对你的壮举感激不尽。

source: See here, I have marked the last known position on your sea chart. @l$Pos$ Find and destroy this convoy. You have until @D$EndDate$.
text: 看，我已经在您的海图上标出了最后获知的位置。@l$Pos$ 找到并摧毁这支船队。您的期限是@D$EndDate$。

source: You must act quickly. The convoy's current position has been marked on your sea chart. @l$Pos$ You have until @D$EndDate$ to find and destroy this convoy.
text: 必须尽快行动。船队当前位置已标在海图上。@l$Pos$ 请在@D$EndDate$之前找到并消灭它。

source: Thank you! You must hurry, for it will be very difficult to locate the convoy if it has chosen a new region as its destination. Its last position has been marked on your sea chart. @l$Pos$ You have until @D$EndDate$.
text: 谢谢！你必须抓紧时间，一旦那支船队改道前往新的海域，就很难再找到它了。我已在海图上标出它最后出现的位置。@l$Pos$你的期限是@D$EndDate$。

source: You have conquered the legendary treasure fleet.
text: 你征服了传说中的宝船队。

source: Good. The ship went down somewhere along the route between @T$TOWN$ and @T$Town$. Please hurry! The chances of finding any survivors after @D$EndDate$ are slim.<n>By the way, there is a shortage of workers in @T$SampleTown$ at the moment. You could simply put the survivors ashore there.
text: 好。船沉在@T$TOWN$和@T$Town$之间的航路上。请抓紧！过了@D$EndDate$，找到幸存者的希望就很渺茫了。<n>顺便说一句，@T$SampleTown$目前缺少工人，你可以直接把幸存者送到那里上岸。

source: That helps us greatly. Search the route between @T$TOWN$ and @T$Town$. You must have completed your search by @D$EndDate$.<n>If you find any survivors, you can put them ashore in @T$SampleTown$.
text: 这对我们帮助很大。请搜寻@T$TOWN$与@T$Town$之间的航路，并在@D$EndDate$之前完成。<n>如果发现幸存者，可以把他们送到@T$SampleTown$上岸。

source: Thank you! The settlers were on their way to @T$TOWN$ and intended to travel on to @T$Town$. Search the area around these towns until @D$EndDate$, as the ship may have sunk and there may be survivors.
text: 谢谢！移民原本正前往@T$TOWN$，之后打算再去@T$Town$。请在@D$EndDate$之前搜查这两座城镇附近的海域：船可能已经沉没，也许还有幸存者。

source: It is good to see you here.

So the ships are in the harbor. I thank you. I will have a new military convoy assembled immediately.<n>This time, I shall not reward you with gold, for you have plenty of that already.<n>Instead, I shall give you a map on which I have marked the location of a sunken transport convoy. There you shall find a vast quantity of goods.
text: 船只已经到港了，感谢你。我会立即组建新的军事船队。<n>这次我不奖赏金币了，毕竟你已经很富有。<n>我会送你一张地图，上面标出了某支沉没运输船队的位置。那里有大量货物等着你打捞。

source: So the ships are in the harbor. I thank you. I will have a new military convoy assembled immediately.<n>As I said before, my resources are currently very limited and I regret that I cannot reward you with gold. However, your reward is no less valuable.<n>Here, take this map instead. I have marked on it the location of a sunken transport convoy. There you shall find a vast quantity of goods.
text: 船已经停在港口了。谢谢你，我马上就会组建一支新的军事船队。<n>正如我先前所说，我目前的财力十分有限，遗憾的是无法用金币酬谢你。不过，你得到的报酬同样珍贵。<n>来，收下这张地图。我在上面标出了一支沉没的运输船队的位置，你会在那里找到大量货物。

source: %1,<n>greetings. Come on in, we may have something to discuss.
text: %1，<n>你好。请进，我们或许有事可谈。

source: %1,<n>greetings. Let me have a quick look through my documents, so I can see if I have something for you.
text: %1：<n>你好。让我翻一下文件，看看有没有适合交给你的事情。

source: I regret that I cannot tell you exactly where to find it. @l$Pos$ Please bring me the package by @D$EndDate$, you will then receive a handsome reward.
text: 遗憾的是，我无法告诉你它的确切位置。@l$Pos$请在@D$EndDate$之前把包裹带给我，届时你将获得丰厚的报酬。

source: Thank you. I cannot tell you exactly where to find the chest. @l$Pos$ You must search around this area. Return my personal effects by @D$EndDate$.
text: 谢谢。我无法告诉你木箱的确切位置。@l$Pos$ 你需要在这一带搜寻。请在@D$EndDate$之前把我的私人物品带回来。

source: You have failed to breach the defenses of the pirate hideout.
text: 你未能突破海盗巢穴的防线。

source: Well done! The plague in Tortuga is over and the population has been restored to @I$Pop$.<n>You accomplished this mission within @I$Days$ days.
text: 干得好！托尔图加的瘟疫已经结束，人口也恢复到了@I$Pop$。<n>你在@I$Days$天内完成了任务。

source: A local trader is prepared to pay you %1 for the business and all crop fields.
text: 一位当地商人愿意出%1收购这家企业及全部农田。

source: A gold mine has been discovered close to %1. The quality of life has risen as a result and the consumption of luxury goods is twice as high for one month.
text: %1附近发现了一座金矿。当地生活水平随之提高，未来一个月内，奢侈品的消耗量翻倍。

source: I am faced with a problem. I must have a constant stock of @G$Goods$ for the transport convoys.
text: 我遇到了难题，必须持续备好@G$Goods$，供应运输船队。

source: However, the war with @n$FoeNation$ has made this difficult. Can you help me?
text: 不过，与@n$FoeNation$的战争让事情变得棘手。你能帮我吗？

source: Increase your trading profits in the town of Cartagena and obtain a building permit from the master builder.
text: 提高你在卡塔赫纳的贸易利润，并向建筑师取得建筑许可证。

source: Congratulations! You have achieved your objective and made more money. You have also reached a higher rank.<n><n>Your rank is always determined by your total assets. These comprise cash as well as property, such as goods and ships. You can check your wealth at any time under "Successes" in the log. This will also tell you when you'll reach the next rank.<n><n>The higher your rank, the more convoys you can command and, therefore, the greater the number of towns in which you can establish businesses later.<n><n>Now that you have a higher rank, you should assemble another convoy and continue trading to increase your wealth.<n><n>You can check your wealth at any time by positioning your cursor on the blue bar indicating your wealth, which is displayed under this window. <n><n><n><c><f:fonts/ELGRECO_26x26aaFHk.res>Scenario objective<f:fonts/Tiepolo_bold14x14aaFH.res><n><n><c>Assemble a second convoy and increase your total assets to @g$GoldGoal$.
text: 恭喜！你达成目标，赚到了更多钱，也晋升了等级。<n><n>你的等级始终由总资产决定，包括现金，以及货物、船只等财产。随时打开日志中的“成就”，都能查看财富，也能得知何时晋升下一级。<n><n>等级越高，能指挥的船队就越多，将来能开办产业的城镇也就越多。<n><n>既然已经晋升，就应该再组建一支船队，继续贸易，增加财富。<n><n>把鼠标移到本窗口下方表示财富的蓝色进度条上，也能随时查看财富数值。<n><n><n><c><f:fonts/ELGRECO_26x26aaFHk.res>关卡目标<f:fonts/Tiepolo_bold14x14aaFH.res><n><n><c>组建第二支船队，并把总资产提高到@g$GoldGoal$。

source: Should I sign on to this convoy? The previous captain will then retire to the inn.
text: 要我加入这支船队吗？原船长会离职，回到酒馆。

source: This action disbands the convoy and moves goods, cargo and boarding crew to the other convoy. The captain is dismissed and the Transfer window is closed. Do you want to choose this option?
text: 此操作会解散当前船队，并将商品、货物和接舷战船员转入另一支船队。船长将被解雇，调配窗口也会关闭。确定执行吗？

source: Greetings, @A$USER$. I must deliver a large consignment of @G$Goods$ to @T$Town$ but, unfortunately, my captain has let me down. I propose the following plan: You pay me a surety of @g$PriceBuy$, transport @a$Amount$ to @T$Town$ and there you will receive @g$PriceSell$ in return. What say you?
text: 你好，@A$USER$。我必须向@T$Town$运送一大批@G$Goods$，可惜我的船长让我失望了。我有个提议：你先付我@g$PriceBuy$作为保证金，再将@a$Amount$货物运到@T$Town$，到那里就能领到@g$PriceSell$。你觉得如何？

source: I am glad to see you, @A$USER$. You have a large trading fleet don't you? It's just that I have to ship @A$Amount$ of @G$Goods$.<n>How about you pay me a surety of @g$PriceBuy$ and take the goods to @T$Town$. There, you will be able to sell the goods for @g$PriceSell$.
text: 见到你真高兴，@A$USER$。你有一支庞大的商船队，对吧？我正好需要运送@A$Amount$的@G$Goods$。<n>不如你交给我@g$PriceBuy$保证金，把货物运到@T$Town$，然后在那里以@g$PriceSell$出售。

source: I'm in an awkward position. I have until @D$EndDate$ to deliver @a$Amount$ of @G$Goods$ to @T$Town$, but my convoy is already underway with another delivery of goods. I'll make you the following offer: Pay me a surety of @g$PriceBuy$ and deliver the goods. You will then receive @g$PriceSell$ in return. What do you say to that?
text: 我遇上了难题。我必须在@D$EndDate$之前把@a$Amount$的@G$Goods$送到@T$Town$，可我的船队已经出发运送另一批货了。不如这样：你交给我@g$PriceBuy$保证金，并负责送货，之后就能收到@g$PriceSell$。你看如何？

source: We have been able to discover the pirate hideout of %1.  %2 How would you like to attack the hideout and destroy this mob for once and for all and thereby restore some semblance of peace to our waters?
text: 我们发现了%1的海盗巢穴。%2 您愿意进攻巢穴，将这群暴徒一举铲除，让我们的海域重获几分安宁吗？

source: Have you heard that we have finally learned where pirate %1 has his hideout? %2 %3 is looking for a brave hero to destroy it. Are you up to the job?
text: 听说了吗？我们终于查明了海盗%1的巢穴位置。%2 %3正在寻找一位勇士将它摧毁。您愿意担此重任吗？

source: The location of the base that the notorious pirate %1 operates from is no longer a mystery. %2 We should crush this gang to pieces without further delay. I think you are just the man for this job.
text: 臭名昭著的海盗%1从哪里出没，如今已经不再是秘密。%2 我们该立刻把这帮匪徒彻底消灭。我想您正是执行这项任务的合适人选。

source: You have a very good reputation with my nation. However, I know of one way you could improve your reputation even more.<n><n>The hideout of the pirate %1 was discovered a short time ago.  %2<n><n>Perhaps you are the one who will finally rid us all of the scourge of this gang.
text: 你在我国享有很高的声望。不过，我知道一个能让你声望更上一层楼的办法。<n><n>不久前，我们发现了海盗%1的巢穴。%2<n><n>也许你就是那个能彻底铲除这伙祸害的人。

source: Find and destroy the Spanish treasure fleet. It was last in @T$StartTown$, from there it set sail for @T$DestTown$.
text: 找到并消灭西班牙宝船队。它最近停靠@T$StartTown$，随后驶向@T$DestTown$。

source: What a calamity! Have you visited @F$WifeName$ yet today? You can spare yourself the trouble, for she has gone. Look, I found a farewell letter of sorts. She writes that she is fed up with her dull life and that she has eloped with an adventurer. You must rescue my beloved daughter for me!
text: 真是灾难！你今天去看过@F$WifeName$了吗？不必去了，她已经走了。看，我找到了一封像是告别信的东西。她写道，自己受够了乏味的生活，已经跟一个冒险家私奔。你一定要替我救回心爱的女儿！

source: Disaster has struck and it appears to me that you are in the thick of it. My daughter has been abducted by pirates, but someone has left you a message with a map showing the location of a particular spot. It looks to me like a trap, but what are we to do? You have to rescue my daughter!
text: 大事不好，而且看来您也被卷进来了。我的女儿遭海盗绑架了，可有人给您留下一封信，还附了张标着某个地点的地图。我看这像是个圈套，但我们还能怎么办？您必须救出我的女儿！

source: Ha! My daughter, and your wife, has eloped with one of my officers of the town guard! I might have guessed! Now they are both missing, having stolen one of my ships! You must return my daughter to me and make her see reason! Strangely enough, I came across a map on which a place is marked in my daughter's apartments.
text: 哈！我的女儿，也就是您的妻子，竟跟我的一名城卫军军官私奔了！我早该料到！他们偷走我的一艘船，如今都不见了！您必须把我女儿带回来，让她清醒清醒！说来也怪，我在她的房间里找到了一张地图，上面标着一个地点。

source: I thank you on behalf of my nation. The convoy will now be licked into shape and the crew will be assembled. It will be ready to set sail in 15 days.<n><n>If you want to hand over another convoy, you must wait until then.
text: 我代表我国感谢你。现在将整备船队、召集船员，15天后即可启航。<n><n>若想移交另一支船队，请等到那时。

source: Your captain has won his duel with the commander. Your sailors make their way to the treasure chamber and make off with %1.<n><n>Now choose what goods you want to loot from the town's warehouse.
text: 你的船长在与指挥官的决斗中获胜。水手们进入藏宝室，夺走了%1。<n><n>现在请选择要从城镇仓库中劫掠哪些货物。

source: Our enemy, @n$HostileNation$, will stop at nothing. My wife has been abducted and certain conditions have been attached to her release. However, I happen to know where she is being held. Officially, I can do nothing, you understand, but you could attack the town and bring her back to me.
text: 我们的敌人@n$HostileNation$无所不用其极。我的妻子遭到绑架，他们还开出了释放条件。不过，我恰好知道她被关在哪里。你也明白，我不能公开行动，但你可以攻打那座城镇，把她带回来。

source: I am glad to see you.<n>My wife recently received a groomed poodle from Paris. The wretched animal has driven me to distraction, but my wife is besotted with the dog.<n>Somebody learned of this, kidnapped the dog and handed it over to our enemies as a way of blackmailing us.<n><n>Can you rescue the poodle for me?
text: 很高兴见到您。<n>我妻子最近收到了一只从巴黎送来的贵宾犬，还精心修剪过毛。那可恶的畜生简直让我发疯，可我妻子却爱它爱得不得了。<n>有人得知此事后，绑走了那条狗，还把它交给我们的敌人，想借此要挟我们。<n><n>您能帮我把贵宾犬救回来吗？

source: Some time ago, my youngest daughter ran off with some sort of passing adventurer, it was said at the time. I have now discovered that she is living in @T$TargetTown$ and that she is to marry the commander of the town. I know my daughter, she would never do such a thing of her own free will! I can hardly suggest to the viceroy that we have to attack a town to rescue my daughter? But how about you?
text: 前些日子，我的小女儿跟某个路过的冒险家私奔了，至少当时人们都是这么说的。如今我发现她住在@T$TargetTown$，还准备嫁给那座城镇的指挥官。我了解自己的女儿，她绝不会自愿做出这种事！我总不能向殖民地总督提议，为救女儿而攻打一座城镇吧？不过，你是否愿意出手？

source: Once you own businesses, you can check here to see if production problems have occurred.
name: IDPR_LOP_NO_PRODUCTION
text: 拥有产业后，你可以在这里检查生产是否出现问题。

source: Find the pirate convoy commanded by @P$PirateName$, which is located approximately 1 day’s journey northeast of Providence. Destroy this convoy.<n>Then return to the Governor of Cartagena.
text: 找到@P$PirateName$指挥的海盗船队，它位于普罗维登斯东北方向约一天航程处。消灭这支船队。<n>然后返回卡塔赫纳总督那里。

source: You have been assigned the mission of tracking down and destroying one of Blackbeard's pirate convoys.<n><n>Blackbeard has a secret hideout where he keeps several convoys, each consisting of five fully-armed ships. This will be a difficult mission for the convoy you have at present.<n><n>Therefore, you should first increase your convoy's firepower. To get enough money to purchase a bigger ship, you can sell the goods from your warehouse in @T$TOWN$ at the best prices you can get. Follow the tips in the Event window, which tell you where you can sell the goods at a good price to the north and east of @T$TOWN$.<n><n>Don't spend too much time on this, as you still have to accomplish the governor's mission afterwards!<n><n><n><f:fonts/ELGRECO_26x26aaFHk.res>Scenario objective<f:fonts/Tiepolo_bold14x14aaFH.res><n><n><c>Sell the goods in your warehouse in @T$TOWN$ and increase your cash to @g$GoldGoal$.
text: 你接到的任务是追踪并消灭黑胡子的一支海盗船队。<n><n>黑胡子在秘密藏身处驻有数支船队，每支都由五艘全副武装的船组成。以你目前的船队实力，完成这项任务并不容易。<n><n>因此，你应先增强船队的火力。为了凑够购买更大战舰的钱，可以把你在@T$TOWN$仓库里的货物尽量卖个好价钱。留意事件窗口中的提示，它会告诉你在@T$TOWN$以北和以东的哪些地方能以高价出售货物。<n><n>别在这上面耽搁太久，你还得完成总督的任务！<n><n><n><f:fonts/ELGRECO_26x26aaFHk.res>剧本目标<f:fonts/Tiepolo_bold14x14aaFH.res><n><n><c>出售@T$TOWN$仓库中的货物，将现金增加到@g$GoldGoal$。

source: Tips on buying and selling goods
We are at war with @n$TargetNation$ and, in light of recent events, the time has now come for us to retaliate. I want you to capture or sink military ships on my behalf. Do you accept this mission?
text: 我们正与@n$TargetNation$交战。鉴于最近发生的事情，现在是反击的时候了。我希望你替我俘获或击沉军事船只。你接受这项任务吗？

source: Just recently, @n$TargetNation$ attacked one of our towns. Now I'm planning my own military action against @n$TargetNation$ and was wondering if you'd like to be part of it? I want you to sink or capture military convoys. Everything you loot from them is yours to keep, all I care about is weakening @n$TargetNation$. Are you interested?
text: 不久前，@n$TargetNation$袭击了我们的一座城镇。如今我正计划对@n$TargetNation$展开军事行动，不知你是否愿意参与？我要你击沉或夺取军事船队。劫获的一切全归你，我只关心削弱@n$TargetNation$的实力。你有兴趣吗？

source: One of our towns has been attacked by @n$TargetNation$. We are now retaliating and sinking their ships. I would very much like to send you to a particular area and authorize you to capture or sink military ships.
text: 我国一座城镇遭到@n$TargetNation$袭击。我们正在报复，击沉他们的船。我想派你前往一片指定海域，授权你俘获或击沉敌方军舰。

source: Then set off on your journey. Head for the waters off the town of @T$TargetTown$.
text: 那就出发吧，驶向@T$TargetTown$城镇外的海域。

source: You have until @D$EndDate$ to complete this mission.
text: 你必须在@D$EndDate$之前完成这项任务。

source: and may now control 2 captains and own 1 permit.
text: 现在可以雇用2名船长，并拥有1张许可证。

source: and may now control %1 captains and own %2 permits.
text: 现在可以雇用%1名船长，并拥有%2张许可证。

source: and may now control any number of captains and own 10 permits.
text: 现在可以指挥任意数量的船长，并拥有10张建筑许可证。

source: and may now control any number of captains and permits.
text: 现在，你可拥有的船长和许可证数量已不受限制。

source: You start the game with the rank of Sailor in the Spanish governor town of @T$TOWN$, where you already have a warehouse. You also have a convoy in the harbor with two armed ships but no sailors.<n><n>The first objective in this scenario is to visit the Governor of @T$TOWN$ and accept his mission. He is having problems with the notorious pirate, Edward Teach, better known as Blackbeard, and wants you to help him.<n><n>Important: The nations are at peace in this scenario. This means that you must never attack a convoy belonging to a nation.<n><n><n><f:fonts/ELGRECO_26x26aaFHk.res>Scenario objective<f:fonts/Tiepolo_bold14x14aaFH.res><n><n><c>Visit the Governor of @T$TOWN$ and accept the mission he assigns to you.
text: 游戏开始时，你是一名水手，身处西班牙总督驻地@T$TOWN$，并已拥有一座仓库。港口里还有一支由两艘武装船组成的船队，不过船上没有水手。<n><n>本剧本的首个目标是拜访@T$TOWN$总督，接受他的委托。他正为臭名昭著的海盗爱德华·蒂奇——也就是黑胡子——而烦恼，希望你能帮助他。<n><n>重要：本剧本中各国处于和平状态。这意味着，你绝不能袭击任何国家所属的船队。<n><n><n><f:fonts/ELGRECO_26x26aaFHk.res>剧本目标<f:fonts/Tiepolo_bold14x14aaFH.res><n><n><c>拜访@T$TOWN$总督，并接受他交给你的任务。

source: Production and consumption by your own businesses
text: 自有企业的生产与消耗

source: New building land is now available there.
text: 那里现在有新的建筑用地可用。

source: <g:INTEXT_SCHATZKISTE_800x600.screen><n>You have found a treasure chest in the water.<n><n>@g$Gold$

A number of traders have joined forces and are demanding greater protection in our waters. To back up their demands, they have decided to stop supplying one of our towns soon. Can you intervene to help me and the citizens?
text: 一些商人联合起来，要求我们加强海域保护。为施压，他们决定很快停止向我国一座城镇供货。你能出面帮助我和那里的居民吗？

source: One of our towns now hardly sees a trader from one end of the week to the next, because a rumor has spread that a plague has hit the town. Can you help me to quash the rumor by supplying the town with goods?
text: 有人散布瘟疫袭击城镇的谣言，害得我国一座城镇整周几乎见不到商人。你能向那里供应商品，帮我粉碎这个谣言吗？

source: The threat of a plague has loomed over one of our towns in recent weeks. To make matters worse, the traders are giving the town a wide berth now as well. Can you help support the town until the situation improves?
text: 近几周，我国一座城镇一直笼罩在瘟疫威胁下。更糟的是，商人如今也远远避开那里。你能持续支援城镇，直到情况好转吗？

source: A citizen died of a plague in one of our towns a few days ago. We tried to cover it up, but I'm afraid word still got out. Now many traders have decided not to call at the town. You have a fine trading fleet. Couldn't you supply the town for the next while?
text: 几天前，我国一座城镇有个居民死于瘟疫。我们试图隐瞒此事，可消息恐怕还是传了出去。现在许多商人都不肯来这座城镇了。您有一支出色的商船队，能在这段时间替城里运送物资吗？

source: Your warships have forced the attackers to flee.
text: 你的战船迫使袭击者逃跑。

source: You have attacked a convoy belonging to a friendly nation. In this scenario, the nations are at peace, which means that you must on no account attack traders or military convoys.
text: 你攻击了友好国家的船队。本关中各国处于和平状态，因此绝不能攻击商人或军事船队。

source: You've now learned how to buy and sell goods. You should always buy goods in the towns where they are produced, as they are generally less expensive there.<n><n>Note: If you want to trade with a convoy, you must have selected it and it must already be in the town before you enter the docks.<n><n>Later in this scenario, you should make profits by trading on your own. The Event window contains tips for doing this.<n><n><n><c><f:fonts/ELGRECO_26x26aaFHk.res>Scenario objective<f:fonts/Tiepolo_bold14x14aaFH.res><n><n><c>You must make @g$GoldGoal$ in cash from trade.
text: 你已经学会买卖货物。尽量在货物的产地采购，因为那里通常价格更低。<n><n>注意：若要通过船队进行贸易，进入码头之前必须先选中该船队，并确保它已停靠本城。<n><n>接下来的剧本中，你需要自行开展贸易获利。事件窗口会提供相关提示。<n><n><n><c><f:fonts/ELGRECO_26x26aaFHk.res>剧本目标<f:fonts/Tiepolo_bold14x14aaFH.res><n><n><c>通过贸易获得@g$GoldGoal$现金。

source: Should I sign on to this ship and assemble a new convoy?
text: 要我到这艘船上任职，并组建新船队吗？

source: Your captain has lost the duel and the ship.
text: 您的船长输掉了决斗，也丢掉了船。

source: Secure the route of the transport convoy that will be leaving the harbor of @T$TOWN$ on @D$DepartDate$ bound for Europe. The convoy must not be attacked. Afterwards, report to the governor of @T$TOWN$.
text: 保障运输船队的航路安全。该船队将于@D$DepartDate$从@T$TOWN$港口启航前往欧洲，途中不得遭到攻击。事后向@T$TOWN$总督复命。

source: The welfare of @T$TargetTown$ is very close to my heart, but I'm afraid the town's economy has been in difficulty for some time. The problem is always the same: Traders stop calling at the town because demand is too low and the goods the town produces are not collected. This makes the town unattractive for new settlers. Will you help me get the town back on its feet?
text: 我一直很关心@T$TargetTown$的福祉，可惜这座城镇的经济已经困难了一段时间。问题总是如此：需求太低，商人就不再停靠，城里生产的货物也无人收购。这使得城镇无法吸引新的移民。你愿意帮我让它重新振作起来吗？

source: I have managed to plant a spy on board an English ship.
text: 我成功在一艘英格兰船上安插了一名间谍。

source: I have managed to plant a spy on board a French ship.
text: 我成功地在一艘法国船上安插了一名间谍。

source: I have managed to plant a spy on board a Dutch ship.
text: 我成功在一艘荷兰船上安插了一名间谍。

source: I have managed to plant a spy on board a Spanish ship
text: 我成功在一艘西班牙船上安插了一名间谍。

source: You should be able to find him there in the next couple of months.
text: 接下来几个月，你应该都能在那里找到他。
消灭一支英格兰军事船队。

source: The game "One-Armed Pirate" is a game of chance with 32 cards. Each player puts their stake in the pot and is given 5 cards, which the other player cannot see.<n><n>First, each player must call the number of points they think they can win, where each trick won equals one point. The player who calls the higher number of points leads the game and decides the trump suit. He must now try to win at least that number of points.<n><n>The player who leads plays his first cards and the other player must follow by playing a card of the same suit, if he can. The player with the highest card wins the point.<n><n>If a player cannot follow suit, he can discard any card or play a trump card.<n><n>The sequence of the cards is I, II, III, IV, Pirate, Bride, Governor, Parrot. A trump card beats all other cards.<n><n>The player who has won the point plays the next card. You continue like this until someone wins the game.<n><n>If the leader succeeds in winning the number of points he called, he wins the game and takes the pot. If he doesn't, his opponent wins.
text: “独臂海盗”是一种使用32张牌的博弈游戏。双方把赌注放入彩池，各拿五张牌，不能让对方看见。<n><n>首先，双方分别叫出自己预计能赢得的分数，每赢一墩得一分。叫分较高者成为主叫方，决定王牌花色，并且必须争取至少赢得所叫的分数。<n><n>主叫方先出牌，对方若有同花色的牌，就必须跟出同花色。牌面较大者赢得这一分。<n><n>如果没有同花色的牌，可以垫任意一张牌，也可以打出王牌。<n><n>牌的大小顺序为：I、II、III、IV、海盗、新娘、总督、鹦鹉。王牌大于其他花色的牌。<n><n>赢得本墩的人接着出牌，如此继续，直到分出胜负。<n><n>若主叫方拿到至少所叫的分数，就赢得本局并拿走彩池；否则由对手获胜。

source: Find a chest by @D$EndDate$ for @N$ContactName$ in @T$ContactTown$. @l$ChestPos$
Find and destroy one of Blackbeard's pirate convoys.
text: 找到并消灭黑胡子的一支海盗船队。

source: Find and destroy one of Blackbeard's pirate convoys. You have until @D$EndDate$.
text: 找到并消灭黑胡子的一支海盗船队。期限为@D$EndDate$。

source: The most important factors influencing the quality of life in a town are the supply and range of goods available. However, you don't have to ensure supplies of all kinds of goods to keep the inhabitants happy.<n><n>The goods in a town can be divided into five groups: essential goods, raw materials, finished goods, colonial goods and import goods. These are listed in the same sequence in the Trade window. A sufficient supply of two to three goods in each group will ensure a good quality of life in your town. <n><n>You have just received a message on the subject of the quality of life in towns. You can display this in the log.<n><n>Because your town is still small, it is particularly easy to achieve a good quality of life because the citizens of small towns are not too demanding. This means that you shouldn't have any problems achieving your objective. However, a town with fewer than 2,000 inhabitants cannot rise above the status “boom”.<n><n><n><f:fonts/ELGRECO_26x26aaFHk.res>Scenario objective<f:fonts/Tiepolo_bold14x14aaFH.res><n><n><c>Ensure that your town has a supply of five barrels of each good.
text: 决定城镇生活质量的最重要因素，是商品供应是否充足、品种是否丰富。不过，要让居民满意，并不需要每一种商品都供应齐全。<n><n>城镇的商品分为五类：生活必需品、原材料、制成品、殖民地商品和进口商品。贸易窗口也按此顺序排列。每一类中有两三种商品供应充足，就能让城镇保持良好的生活质量。<n><n>你刚刚收到一条关于城镇生活质量的消息，可以在日志中查看。<n><n>你的城镇还很小，小城镇的居民要求不高，因此很容易改善生活质量，完成目标应该并不困难。但人口不足2,000的城镇，发展状态最高只能达到“繁荣”。<n><n><n><f:fonts/ELGRECO_26x26aaFHk.res>关卡目标<f:fonts/Tiepolo_bold14x14aaFH.res><n><n><c>确保你的城镇每种商品都有五桶库存。

source: Good. The two abandoned ships I want you to dispose of are located approximately two days north of Cartagena.
text: 好。我希望你处理掉的那两艘弃船，在卡塔赫纳以北约两天航程处。

source: Excellent! The convoy of pirate @P$PirateName$ is located near the town of Belize, which is approximately 5 days’ journey northwest of here This town is in the northwest. Then return here to bring me news of your success.
text: 太好了！海盗@P$PirateName$的船队就在伯利兹附近。从这里向西北航行大约五天就能抵达那座城镇，它位于西北部。成功后请回来向我报喜。

source: A little more than 1 day’s journey west of Cartagena is the small island of Providence. The pirate convoy commanded by @P$PirateName$ was last seen there. You should find the pirate convoy commanded by @P$PirateName$ approximately 1 day’s journey northeast of there.<n>Destroy it and then return here to give me a full account of the events.
text: 从卡塔赫纳向西航行一天多，就是普罗维登斯小岛。@P$PirateName$指挥的海盗船队最近在那里出现。你应该能在其东北方约一天航程处，找到@P$PirateName$的船队。<n>消灭它，然后回来详细向我汇报。

source: You have not completed the mission I gave you.
text: 您还没有完成我交给您的任务。

source: Why did you not complete the last mission I gave you?
text: 你为什么没有完成我上次交给你的任务？

source: I am very angry with you because you failed to accomplish the mission I gave you.
text: 你没能完成我交给你的任务，对此我十分生气。

source: The deadline for the goods handover has expired.

Greetings, %1. Shall I arrange a feast for you in our town? It will improve prosperity in this town for a time and will enhance your reputation in my nation.<n><n>The feast shall be held no later than %2.<n><n>How lavish should the feast be?
text: 您好，%1。要我替您在城里安排一场宴会吗？它能暂时提高本城的繁荣程度，并提升您在我国的声望。<n><n>宴会最迟将在%2举行。<n><n>您打算办得多盛大？

source: Greetings, %1. Shall I arrange a feast for you in our town? It will improve prosperity in this town for a time and will help you to obtain a building permit.<n><n>The feast shall be held no later than %2.<n><n>How lavish should the feast be?
text: 你好，%1。要我替你在本城安排一场宴会吗？它能暂时提高城镇繁荣度，也有助于你获得建筑许可证。<n><n>宴会最迟于%2举行。<n><n>你希望宴会办得多丰盛？

source: The number of citizens (the population minus the number of soldiers) in Tortuga must be restored to @I$Pop$ within 20 days of the plague ending to ensure that all businesses have a full complement of workers.
text: 瘟疫结束后20天内，必须将托尔图加的市民人数（总人口减去士兵人数）恢复到@I$Pop$，以确保所有企业都有充足的工人。

source: <ts:80>Due to wear and tear, a %1 D774has sunk today on the trade route.<n><n>Losses:<n><n>Goods:<t>%2<n>Cannons:<t>%3<n>Sailors:<t>%4<n><n>Pay more attention to the condition of your ships. You can also activate automatic repairs for trade routes.
text: <ts:80>由于失修，一艘%1今天在贸易航线上沉没。<n><n>损失：<n><n>货物：<t>%2<n>火炮：<t>%3<n>水手：<t>%4<n><n>请多注意船只状况。你也可以为贸易航线启用自动维修。

source: <ts:80>Due to wear and tear, your convoy lost a %1 today.<n><n>Losses:<n><n>Goods:<t>%2<n>Cannons:<t>%3<n>Sailors:<t>%4<n><n>Pay more attention to the condition of your ships. You can also activate automatic repairs for trade routes.<n>
text: <ts:80>由于失修，你的船队今天损失了一艘%1。<n><n>损失：<n><n>货物：<t>%2<n>火炮：<t>%3<n>水手：<t>%4<n><n>请多注意船只状况。你也可以为贸易航线启用自动维修。<n>

source: If you want to purchase a business or residential building from a local trader, you must have both a building permit and a warehouse in the town.
text: 要向当地商人购买产业或住宅建筑，你必须同时拥有该城镇的建筑许可证和仓库。

source: Everyone has been given 5 cards. I’ll call 5 points.<n><n><n>Since you cannot beat that, the game is mine!
text: 每人拿到五张牌。我叫五分。<n><n><n>你不可能叫得更高，所以这局由我主叫！

source: Pay a visit to the Governor of @T$TOWN$ and collect your reward.
I will tell my men immediately so that they can put to sea. Come back in a few weeks, maybe I will have the first share for you then!
text: 我马上通知手下，让他们出海。几周后再来吧，也许到时就能给你第一笔分红了！

source: Build a cotton production facility in Santa Marta and increase your cash to @g$GoldGoal$ from trade.
text: 在圣玛尔塔建造棉花生产设施，并通过贸易将现金增加到@g$GoldGoal$。

source: Lasmiranda stirbt vor langer Weile! Sie sitzt seit vielen Tagen am Cap und winkt vorbeifahrenden Schiffe zu. Es sei aber noch kein wilder Pirat bei ihr vorgefahren, berichtet sie.
name: IDPR_TEST_05
text: Lasmiranda快无聊死了！她在海角坐了好多天，不停地向经过的船只挥手。据她说，却还没有一个狂野的海盗驶到她面前。

source: I’d be happy to tell you something of the life of the pirate Henry Avery.
text: 我很乐意给你讲讲海盗亨利·埃弗里的生平。

source: Have you heard of the notorious pirate Edward Teach, otherwise known as Blackbeard?
text: 你听说过臭名昭著的海盗爱德华·蒂奇吗？人们也叫他黑胡子。

source: I could tell you something about the sugar cane plantations.
text: 我可以给你讲讲甘蔗种植园。

source: I’ll tell you what I’ve learned about the slave trade from my own experiences.
text: 我来讲讲自己亲身了解到的奴隶贸易。

source: Have you ever come across the term “indentured labor”? I could tell you something about this.
text: 你听说过“契约劳工”吗？我可以给你讲讲。

source: Let me tell you something about the Navigation Act.
But you yourself are accustomed to sea travel and must be familiar with the illnesses seamen suffer.
text: 你自己也常在海上航行，想必很了解水手容易得的疾病。

source: I have some amusing information for you about the naming of new geographical discoveries.
text: 关于新发现地理事物的命名，我有些趣事可以讲给你听。

source: I’d be happy to give you some information on the viceroys here in the New World.
text: 我很乐意为你讲讲新大陆的殖民地总督。

source: I’d be happy to tell you about some particularly interesting discoveries in the New World.
text: 我很乐意给你讲讲新大陆上一些特别有趣的发现。

source: I can give you some account of the origin of myths and legends.
text: 我可以给你讲讲神话传说的由来。

source: You will surely want to hear about Sir Walter Raleigh, the English writer and adventurer.
text: 你一定想听听英格兰作家兼冒险家沃尔特·雷利爵士的故事。

source: Let me tell you a little about how the American Indian population was treated by the Europeans.
text: 让我给您讲讲欧洲人是如何对待美洲印第安人的。

source: I have some information for you on German involvement in expeditions and on the first Germans in Venezuela.
text: 我有些情报，讲的是德国人参与远征的经历，以及最早到达委内瑞拉的德国人。

source: Let me tell you something about Spain’s riches.
text: 让我给你讲讲西班牙的财富。

source: I’ve just learned something about the Treaty of Tordesillas.
text: 我刚了解到一些关于《托尔德西里亚斯条约》的事情。

source: Surely you have already come face to face with a buccaneer or have already accepted a Letter of Marque?
text: 你肯定已经遇见过私掠者，或领到过私掠许可证了吧？

source: Have you ever come across the term “the seven seas”? I can tell you why it’s actually incorrect!
text: 你听过“七大洋”这个说法吗？我可以告诉你，它为什么其实并不准确！

source: Have you ever visited the Bermuda islands in the far northeast? I can tell you something about them.
text: 你去过遥远东北方的百慕大群岛吗？我可以给你讲讲那里。

source: I’d be happy to tell you a little about the rise of England in the New World.
text: 我很乐意给你讲讲英格兰在新大陆的崛起。

source: I will tell you a little about Columbus’s great voyage across the Atlantic and the discovery of America.
text: 我来给你讲一讲，哥伦布横渡大西洋并发现美洲的伟大航程。

source: Where did America get its name? I can give you the answer.
text: 美洲的名字从何而来？我可以告诉你答案。

source: I will tell you a little about Hispaniola, the first American colony that became very important under Spanish rule.
text: 我来讲讲伊斯帕尼奥拉岛：这是美洲最早的殖民地，在西班牙统治下变得极为重要。

source: I’m sure you also trade in rum? I can tell you something about that.
text: 你一定也做朗姆酒生意吧？我可以给你讲讲它的故事。

source: Let me tell you a little about Jamaica, the island on which the town of Port Royale is situated.
text: 让我给您讲讲皇家港所在的岛屿——牙买加。

source: Let me tell you a little about Cuba, the largest island in the West Indies.
text: 让我给你讲讲古巴，西印度群岛中最大的岛屿。

source: You know that many things that are now quite commonplace in Europe were first discovered in America. But do you know what “gifts” Europe brought to the New World?
text: 你知道，许多如今在欧洲习以为常的东西，最初都发现于美洲。不过，你知道欧洲给新大陆带去了哪些“礼物”吗？

source: Have you ever traded in cocoa? Let me tell you a little about this plant.
text: 你做过可可生意吗？让我给你讲讲这种植物。

source: You might not believe it, but there are female pirates too!
text: 你也许不信，海盗里也有女人！

source: Have you ever heard tell of the Welsh pirate Bartholomew Roberts?
text: 你听说过威尔士海盗巴塞洛缪·罗伯茨吗？

source: I’ve found some information for you about the pirate Henry Morgan. Let me tell you.
text: 我为你找到了些关于海盗亨利·摩根的资料，让我讲给你听。

source: I have some information for you on the Bahamas.
text: 我有一些关于巴哈马的消息告诉您。

source: Let me tell you a little about the social system in the Spanish colonies.
text: 让我给你讲讲西班牙殖民地的社会制度。

source: Greetings to you! I am just drafting a new historical essay.
text: 你好！我正在撰写一篇新的历史文章。

source: Henry Avery is a prime example of the successful pirate. He captured the richest ships of his time, managed to elude the authorities and live long enough to enjoy his wealth.<n><n>Avery's early years are shrouded in mystery. However, we do know that in June 1694 he was a mate on a privateer named Charles, which had been given permission by the Spanish to capture ships belonging to the French colony of Martinique in the West Indies. One day, he led a mutiny and seized control of the ship, whereupon most of the crew sided with him. The ship, a fast privateer with 46 cannons and ideally suited to the role of pirate ship, was renamed Fancy. In 1695, he succeeded in carrying out his greatest feat: The looting of the Indian treasure fleet. As part of an alliance with other pirates, he attacked a heavily armed Indian treasure fleet and managed to capture two ships. The ships belonged to the Grand Mogul himself and were loaded with unimaginable treasures. <n><n>After bribing the governor of the Bahamas to offer the pirates protection, Avery paid off the crew, who then scattered to the four corners of the earth. Some of them were captured in England but Avery sailed to Ireland, where he disappeared without trace. We can only assume that he continued to enjoy his wealth in hiding.
text: 亨利·埃弗里是成功海盗的典范。他夺取了当时最富有的船只，躲过了当局追捕，还活得足够久，得以享受自己的财富。<n><n>埃弗里的早年经历笼罩在迷雾之中。不过，我们知道，1694年6月，他在一艘名为“Charles”的私掠船上担任大副。这艘船获得西班牙许可，可以袭击西印度群岛法国殖民地马提尼克的船只。一天，他发动叛变，夺取了船只，大多数船员都站到了他这一边。这艘配有46门火炮、航速很快的私掠船极适合做海盗船，后来更名为“Fancy”。1695年，他完成了一生中最惊人的壮举：劫掠印度宝船队。他与其他海盗结盟，袭击了一支武装强大的印度宝船队，并成功夺取两艘船。它们属于莫卧儿皇帝本人，船上满载难以想象的珍宝。<n><n>埃弗里贿赂巴哈马总督，为海盗们换取庇护，随后向船员分发钱财。众人就此散往天涯海角，其中一些在英格兰被捕，而埃弗里则驶往爱尔兰，从此消失得无影无踪。我们只能猜想，他后来一直隐姓埋名，享受着自己的财富。

source: One of the most popular pirates of all time was Edward Teach (died 1718), alias Blackbeard, whose hallmark, as his name implies, was his fearsome black plaited beard. With a crew of 300 men, he sailed the high seas in his ship, Queen Anne’s Revenge, a converted Dutch trading ship, and had no fear of taking on the warships of the Royal Navy.<n><n>Over a period of 18 months, Teach, who was born in Bristol, wrought havoc, mainly in the northern part of the West Indies and along the coast of North America. He was always able to find refuge in the Bahamas and in poverty-stricken North Carolina.<n><n>Another reason why Blackbeard was so famous was that he fitted the stereotype of a terrifying, hot-blooded and temperamental buccaneer: He is alleged to have maimed his gunner Israel Hands by shooting him twice, for no reason other than to remind the rest of the crew who was in charge.<n><n>His final hour only arrived in 1718 when the pirate hunter Robert Maynard tracked down his sloop. Despite being roaring drunk, Teach fought like a demon and was only defeated after a bitter struggle. He was killed in the battle and most of the surviving members of his crew were hanged.
text: 有史以来最著名的海盗之一，是绰号“黑胡子”的爱德华·蒂奇（卒于1718年）。顾名思义，他最醒目的标志就是那副编成辫子的吓人黑胡须。他率领300名船员，驾驶由荷兰商船改装的“安妮女王复仇号”纵横大洋，连皇家海军的战舰也敢正面交锋。<n><n>这位出生于布里斯托尔的海盗，在18个月里主要肆虐于西印度群岛北部和北美沿岸。他总能在巴哈马和贫困的北卡罗来纳找到庇护。<n><n>黑胡子出名的另一个原因，是他完全符合人们对海盗的想象：可怕、热血、喜怒无常。据说他曾向炮手伊斯雷尔·汉兹开了两枪，令其残废，原因仅仅是要提醒其他船员谁才是老大。<n><n>直到1718年，海盗猎手罗伯特·梅纳德追踪到他的单桅帆船，黑胡子的末日才终于到来。尽管酩酊大醉，蒂奇仍像恶魔般奋战，经过一场惨烈搏斗才被击败。他战死当场，幸存船员中的大多数则被处以绞刑。

source: Those who yearned to add to their existing wealth in the early years of the Age of Discovery found that the sugar plantations that had been developed since the early 16th century, mainly in the Caribbean, offered excellent investment opportunities.<n><n>These investments returned an average profit of ten percent and in the best cases (such as on Barbados around 1650) as much as 50 percent! Naturally, these plantations required huge numbers of workers and so hundreds of thousands of slaves were shipped there from Africa. This was because the white man had by now almost completely exterminated the Native American population in many places. <n><n>The Europeans themselves could not endure the climate and, quite apart from that, they were far too dignified to engage in this sort of donkey work. Even the plantation owners preferred to live in London or Madrid and let a couple of their henchmen organize the work in the colonies. By the 18th century, the black proportion of the population of some islands had reached 90 percent!
text: 大航海时代初期，希望进一步积累财富的人发现，自16世纪初发展起来、主要集中在加勒比地区的甘蔗种植园，是绝佳的投资机会。<n><n>这类投资平均可带来百分之十的利润，最理想的情况下，甚至可达百分之五十，例如1650年前后的巴巴多斯！种植园自然需要大量劳动力，于是数十万奴隶被从非洲运来。这是因为当时白人已在许多地方几乎灭绝了原住民。<n><n>欧洲人自己难以忍受当地气候，而且还自恃身份，不愿从事这类苦役。就连种植园主也更愿意住在伦敦或马德里，只派几个心腹在殖民地管理劳作。到了18世纪，一些岛屿的黑人居民比例已高达百分之九十！

source: The trade in “black gold” had already begun in the early 16th century. The slave traders’ preferred source of “goods” was the coast of West Africa that stretched between the Senegal river and what is today known as Cameroon. Not only was this area ideally situated from a transport point of view, it also possessed a stable economic and sociopolitical infrastructure. This meant that the sailors did not have to go hunting for slaves themselves, but could purchase their victims from the local chieftains or from other slave traders.<n><n>Young men between the ages of 15 and 35 were particularly sought after because they were destined primarily for hard labor on the plantations. Approximately one in every five slaves didn’t even survive the crossing, which could last for up to six weeks. Some died as a result of the barbaric treatment meted out by their masters, while others perished due to accidents at sea. Taking this high mortality rate into account, the slave traders sought to make each voyage as profitable as possible by cramming as many slaves as they could onto their ships. For weeks on end, these wretched creatures lay side by side like sardines in a tin, chained to one another, in the dark and with barely enough air to breathe.<n><n>Under these conditions, it is almost incredible that any of them survived these journeys!
text: 所谓“黑色黄金”的贸易早在16世纪初就已开始。奴隶贩子最青睐的“货源地”，是塞内加尔河与今天的喀麦隆之间的西非海岸。这里不仅便于运输，而且拥有稳定的经济和社会政治结构。因此，水手不必亲自捕捉奴隶，而可以向当地酋长或其他奴隶贩子购买受害者。<n><n>15至35岁的年轻男性尤其受到追捧，因为他们主要被送往种植园从事繁重劳动。航程最长可达六周，约有五分之一的被贩卖者甚至无法活着渡海。有些人死于奴隶主的野蛮虐待，另一些则葬身海难。为了在如此高的死亡率下仍然尽可能获利，奴隶贩子把尽可能多的人塞进船舱。数周之久，这些可怜的人像罐头中的沙丁鱼一般并排躺着，彼此锁在一起，身处黑暗，连呼吸所需的空气都极为稀薄。<n><n>在这样的条件下，竟然还有人能够活过航程，几乎令人难以置信！

source: Although there were no white slaves in North and Central America, there were plenty of Europeans who found themselves working under conditions that differed very little from those of the slaves.<n><n>Many young men (predominantly from the uneducated lower classes) wanted to emigrate but did not have the money to pay for the crossing. They therefore borrowed the money to pay for their passage, on the understanding that they would then settle the debt by working for a certain period on a sugar plantation (or somewhere similar). <n><n>However, what seemed a perfectly logical arrangement also had a catch: Many plantation owners tried to work these contract workers as hard as they possibly could during their period of employment. Added to this was the Caribbean climate that most Europeans found so hard to endure.<n><n>This system of “indentured labor” was also frequently used for convicts who had been expelled from their native countries. The British used this method later on, most notably against the Indians, whom they forced to work in the African colonies.
text: 虽然北美和中美没有白人奴隶，但不少欧洲人却在与奴隶相差无几的条件下劳作。<n><n>许多年轻人想要移民，却无力支付渡海的船费；他们大多来自未受教育的社会底层。于是，他们借钱支付旅费，并约定抵达后在甘蔗种植园或类似场所劳动一段时间，以偿还债务。<n><n>然而，这种看似合情合理的安排暗藏陷阱：许多种植园主在契约期内竭尽所能地压榨这些劳工。更何况，加勒比地区的气候也让大多数欧洲人难以忍受。<n><n>这种“契约劳工”制度也经常用于被祖国流放的罪犯。英国人后来继续采用这一做法，尤其是强迫印度人前往非洲殖民地劳动。

source: As the American colonies flourished, so too did the trade across the Atlantic Ocean. Great Britain, the most powerful maritime nation since the time of Queen Elizabeth, had a keen interest in controlling the movement of goods, thereby allowing the domestic economy to share in the trading profits.<n><n>Under the Lord Protector, Oliver Cromwell, the “First Navigation Act” of 1651 decreed that only English ships could be used to transport goods from the colonies to Europe. This measure was aimed principally at the emerging power of Holland and benefited the domestic trading fleet.<n><n>In 1663, the provisions of this act were made even more stringent: Colonial ships wishing to transport goods to Europe had to call at English ports and pay a toll there. However, this attempt to control the trade between the colonies soon ran aground. As the British army could scarcely be expected to watch the entire coastline, the result was a flourishing contraband trade. <n><n>It was precisely this ongoing conflict with the mother country regarding the conditions governing the exporting and importing of goods that, particularly in the North American colonies, resulted in the formation of a separate identity among the settlers there and was later to become a significant motivation behind the independence movement.
text: 随着美洲殖民地日益繁荣，横跨大西洋的贸易也蓬勃发展。自伊丽莎白女王时代以来，英国一直是最强大的海上国家，十分热衷于控制货物流动，让本国经济也能分享贸易利润。<n><n>护国公奥利弗·克伦威尔统治时期，1651年的第一部《航海法》规定：殖民地运往欧洲的货物，只能由英格兰船只承运。这项措施主要针对日益崛起的荷兰，使本国商船队从中受益。<n><n>1663年，规定进一步收紧：殖民地船只若要把货物运往欧洲，必须先停靠英格兰港口并缴纳关税。然而，控制殖民贸易的企图很快碰壁。英国军队根本不可能监视整条海岸，结果反而催生了兴盛的走私贸易。<n><n>正是围绕进出口规则与母国持续发生的冲突，使移民形成了独立的身份认同，尤其在北美殖民地如此。这后来成为推动独立运动的重要动因。

source: The beginning of the colonial age brought with it numerous health problems, hitherto largely unknown on the much shorter journeys in the Mediterranean or along the coast. A crossing to the colonies in the Caribbean and North America took from one to two months, or even longer if the ship encountered storms or periods where there was no wind. The difficulties to be overcome were therefore hardly surprising: The stench of filthy clothing and poor personal hygiene, contaminated and rotten food, a lack of clean water, rats on board as well as the psychological strain caused by monotony and cabin fever. The terrible specter of scurvy hung over every seaman: This disease, caused by a lack of vitamins, manifested itself in the loss of hair and teeth and cost many sailors their lives. It was the circumnavigator of the globe, James Cook (1728-1779), who first succeeded in treating this disease. Not only did he insist that the ship be kept clean, he also provided his crew with sauerkraut and fresh fruit. Anyone going ashore also had to contend with tropical diseases such as blackwater fever, one of the most dangerous manifestations of malaria: This infection, whose symptoms include a quickening of the pulse, fever, shivering and dark-colored urine, was almost always fatal.
text: 殖民时代的到来带来了诸多健康问题；此前在地中海或沿岸进行的短途航行中，这些问题大多鲜为人知。横渡大洋前往加勒比海和北美殖民地，通常需要一到两个月，遇上风暴或无风天气则更久。因此，船员面对重重困难也不足为奇：肮脏衣物与个人卫生恶劣带来的臭气，受污染或腐烂的食物，洁净饮水匮乏，船上的鼠患，以及单调生活和狭窄空间造成的精神压力。坏血病的可怕阴影笼罩着每一位水手。这种因缺乏维生素引发的疾病会导致毛发和牙齿脱落，夺去了许多水手的生命。环球航海家詹姆斯·库克（1728—1779）首次成功对付了这种疾病。他不仅要求船上保持清洁，还为船员提供酸菜和新鲜水果。登岸后，人们还必须面对热带疾病，如疟疾最危险的表现之一——黑水热。感染者会出现脉搏加快、发热、寒战和深色尿液，几乎总是难逃一死。

source: There are interesting anecdotes behind the many names that the seafarers and cartographers had to come up with for the new swathes of land, rivers and settlements. Even the first name given by the European explorers of the Age of Discovery in America tells its own story. Christopher Columbus named the island on which he landed on October 12th 1492 Salvador (“Savior“). This was to give thanks to the Lord for protecting the convoy from disease and storms during the outward journey and above all, for preventing a mutiny that threatened to break out literally at the last minute before land was sighted.<n><n>In the times that followed, the Spanish Conquistadors mostly chose names with religious connotations, for example “Nombre de Dios” (“The Name of God“) or “Trinidad” (“Trinity”). In other cases, people took inspiration from the date or from their observations of the landscape. For example, Portuguese sailors named a bay on the Brazilian coast that they discovered on New Year’s Day 1502 “January River” (Rio de Janeiro), and the name of the city of Montevideo refers to Magellan’s alleged exclamation on seeing the coastline for the first time: “Monte vido eu!” (“I see a mountain!”).<n><n>It was also a popular custom for explorers to name swathes of land and towns after their rulers, their mother country or the town from which they came. Not only did this communicate to the outside world a clear statement of tenure, it also created a connection to one’s home country even in these far-flung lands.<n><n>If all else failed, one could always fall back on the names from the native Indian languages (although, in most cases, this did not deter the colonizers from subsequently chasing away or exterminating the natives themselves).<n><n>To this day, the myth persists that, on being asked by James Cook what that strange marsupial was called, an Australian Aborigine replied “kangooroo” or “ganguru”, which allegedly only meant “What are you talking about?”. Even if this is a myth, these kinds of amusing misunderstandings must certainly have taken place. <n><n>One would probably be astonished at how many names of towns, mountains and rivers simply mean “good morning!”, “I beg your pardon?” or “leave me in peace!” ...
text: 航海家和制图师为新发现的陆地、河流与聚落命名时，留下了许多有趣的故事。大航海时代欧洲探险家在美洲取下的第一个地名，就有它自己的来历。克里斯托弗·哥伦布把他于1492年10月12日登陆的岛屿命名为萨尔瓦多，意为“救世主”。这是为了感谢上帝在去程中保佑船队免遭疾病和风暴，尤其是让他们在即将爆发哗变的最后关头看见了陆地。<n><n>此后，西班牙征服者大多选用带有宗教含义的名字，例如“Nombre de Dios”（“上帝之名”）或“Trinidad”（“三位一体”）。有时，人们也会从日期或眼前的地貌中寻找灵感。例如，葡萄牙水手将1502年元旦发现的巴西海岸一处海湾命名为“一月之河”（里约热内卢）；而蒙得维的亚的名称，据说来自麦哲伦初次望见海岸时的惊呼：“Monte vido eu!”（“我看见一座山！”）。<n><n>探险家也常常以自己的君主、祖国或故乡为陆地和城镇命名。这既向外界明确宣示了归属，也让身处遥远异乡的人们与故土保持一份联系。<n><n>实在想不出名字时，还可以借用当地印第安语言中的名称。不过，在大多数情况下，这并没有阻止殖民者随后驱逐或屠杀当地居民。<n><n>直到今天，仍有这样一个传说：詹姆斯·库克询问一种奇怪的有袋动物叫什么时，一位澳大利亚原住民回答了“kangooroo”或“ganguru”，而这句话据说只是“你在说什么？”的意思。即便这只是传说，类似令人忍俊不禁的误会也一定发生过。<n><n>如果知道有多少城镇、山脉和河流的名字其实只是“早上好！”、“你说什么？”或“别来烦我！”，人们大概会大吃一惊……

source: With the emergence of a Spanish empire stretching across the globe, it became necessary to establish colonial authorities with sufficient powers to deal with day-to-day administrative matters as well as any crises that might suddenly arise. For this purpose, the title of viceroy was conferred on the most important governors in the colonies.<n><n>At the height of the world empire, there were two such dignitaries, in New Spain (Mexico) and in Peru. The viceroyalties of New Granada and Rio de la Plata were added during the 18th century.<n><n> The duties of a viceroy (also known as a virrey), which he performed together (and often in conflict) with an administrative council known as the Audiencia, included the normal tasks of a government official: Raising and collecting taxes, ensuring that the population abided by the law, organizing the colony’s defenses and so on. He was also responsible for protecting the Native American population and for the appointment of lesser ecclesiastical and secular dignitaries.<n><n>Due to the enormous economic and political importance of its overseas possessions, the Crown always kept a watchful eye on the activities of its viceroys. They were forbidden from engaging in any extra commercial activities that would earn them an additional income. Quite apart from this, rivalry between the virreys only resulted in the mutual restriction of their power.
text: 随着西班牙帝国的版图遍及全球，王室必须建立拥有充分权力的殖民管理机构，既处理日常政务，也应对突发危机。因此，殖民地最重要的地方长官获授殖民地总督的头衔。<n><n>帝国鼎盛时期，有两位这样的要员，分别驻在新西班牙（墨西哥）和秘鲁。18世纪又增设了新格拉纳达和拉普拉塔总督区。<n><n>殖民地总督在西班牙语中称为 virrey。他与名为 Audiencia 的行政议会共同执政，双方也经常发生冲突。其职责包括制定和征收税款、维护法律、组织殖民地防务等常规政务。此外，他还负责保护美洲原住民，并任命下级宗教和世俗官员。<n><n>海外领地在经济和政治上都极为重要，因此王室始终密切监视殖民地总督的活动。他们不得另行从事商业活动谋取额外收入。而各位总督之间的竞争，也使他们的权力彼此受到牵制。

source: It is already a well known fact that the European conquerors always heeded the call of silver and gold. However, of almost greater value were spices. It is difficult to imagine how dull the European diet of the Middle Ages must have been, if one thinks of the dangers people were prepared to face in order to obtain a little pepper or nutmeg.<n><n>In this regard, the discovery of America proved to be extremely disappointing at first. People noted with interest the exotic animals that Christopher Columbus brought home with him, rejoiced at the expansion of their country’s possessions and at the many souls that they imagined would be saved by the spread of Christianity there. However, the mountains of gold proved rather more elusive than had been promised. These voyages only became profitable ten to twenty years later, when a veritable flood of American silver started to arrive in Europe. <n><n>On one of these voyages, Columbus brought back a treasure more precious than all the gold and silver in the entire world: On the 4th of November 1492, the natives presented him with what he described as an apple that tasted of chestnuts. At that moment, he became the first European to eat a potato! The Indian word for this plant was “batate” and it survives to this day in the English language as “potato”.<n><n>Many other things that we take for granted today were first brought to Europe by Columbus and his successors: Tobacco, tomatoes, corn and the hammock. Or as the Native Americans would say: “hamaka” (from which the English word is derived).
text: 欧洲征服者总是追逐金银，这一点早已众所周知。然而，香料的价值几乎还要更高。想想人们为了弄到一点胡椒或肉豆蔻，竟愿意冒那么大的风险，就很难想象中世纪欧洲人的饮食究竟有多么寡淡。<n><n>从这个角度来说，美洲的发现起初令人极其失望。人们饶有兴趣地观看哥伦布带回的珍奇动物，为国家领土的扩张而欢呼，也想象着基督教的传播将在那里拯救无数灵魂。然而，承诺中的金山却迟迟不见踪影。直到十到二十年后，美洲白银如洪流般涌入欧洲，这些远航才真正开始有利可图。<n><n>在其中一次航行中，哥伦布带回了一件比世上所有金银都更珍贵的宝物：1492年11月4日，当地居民送给他一种东西，被他描述为吃起来像栗子的苹果。就在那一刻，他成了第一个吃到马铃薯的欧洲人！印第安人称这种植物为“batate”，这个词至今仍以英语“potato”的形式保留下来。<n><n>许多今天我们习以为常的东西，最早都是由哥伦布及其继任者带到欧洲的：烟草、番茄、玉米，还有吊床。美洲原住民把吊床叫作“hamaka”，英语中的对应词也由此而来。

source: From the moment it was announced, the discovery of the New World fired the imagination of the people of Europe. What sort of creatures might these unexplored territories contain? The most incredible rumors circulated: One island was said to be teeming with cannibals, the next with headless creatures whose faces were set into their stomachs.<n><n>The South American landscape of Patagonia translates roughly as “land of the big-footed ones” while the Amazon owes its name to a horde of female warriors who are alleged to have reminded the explorers of similar female warriors from Greek mythology.<n><n>While there was a factual background to some of these rumors, others were based on misunderstandings and misinterpretations or on stories that the Native Americans themselves had simply picked up somewhere.<n><n>However, many of these rumors were simply the product of people’s vivid imaginations and, more often than not, people only believed them because they wanted to. This would explain why entire generations of conquistadors searched for the legendary Fountain of Youth, the Garden of Eden and Eldorado, the city of gold. They were encouraged in their erroneous beliefs by the Native Americans, who constantly assured them that they had heard of one place or another, but who simply wished to buy time so they could entice these greedy white men deep inland and cut them off from their ships.
text: 新大陆被发现的消息一经传出，就点燃了欧洲人的想象。这片未经探索的土地上，会有什么样的生物？不可思议的传闻四处流传：一座岛据说满是食人族，另一座岛则住着没有脑袋、脸长在肚子上的怪人。<n><n>南美地名巴塔哥尼亚，大致可译为“大脚人的土地”；亚马孙河则得名于一群女战士，据说她们让探险者想起了希腊神话中的同类人物。<n><n>这些传闻有些确有事实依据，另一些则源于误解和曲解，或是美洲原住民自己也从别处听来的故事。<n><n>不过，许多传闻纯粹出自人们天马行空的想象，而人们往往只因愿意相信，就深信不疑。这也解释了为什么一代代征服者不断寻找传说中的青春之泉、伊甸园和黄金之城埃尔多拉多。原住民不断向他们保证，自己听说过这些地方，进一步助长了他们的错信。原住民其实只是想争取时间，把这些贪婪的白人引向内陆深处，让他们远离自己的船只。

source: One of the most dazzling figures in a list of explorers and conquerors that included many other colorful characters was the English writer and adventurer Sir Walter Raleigh (approx. 1554 – 1618). He first came to prominence in 1580 when he defeated an uprising by Irish rebels opposed to the English occupation.<n><n>He became a favorite of Queen Elizabeth I and used his influence to finance an expedition to find the legendary city of Eldorado in South America. Despite the total failure of several expeditions to find anything of value, he managed to retain the support of his financial backers in London by using his unique powers of persuasion. He gave them to believe that the final prize always lay just beyond the next estuary and that he could not possibly give up now.<n><n>Nevertheless, his credit eventually came to an end. To often, people had listened to his lofty promises only to find out later on that they were nothing but hot air. Raleigh finally fell from grace with Elizabeth. Her successor, James I, saw this hot-blooded adventurer as a threat to his more moderate foreign policy and had him arrested on very weak grounds and sentenced to death as soon as he came to power. His sentence was commuted (mind you, it was not lifted!) and Raleigh was imprisoned in the Tower of London.<n><n>Years later, when the state of the country’s finances persuaded the King that it was necessary, he gave Sir Walter Raleigh permission to lead another expedition to Guyana. This was an absurd situation: giving a man, who was himself sentenced to death, the authority over the life and death of others and sending him off in search of gold! However, this contradiction resolved itself relatively soon afterwards, for Raleigh, by now wracked with fever, lived to see his final expedition end in failure.<n><n>On his return to England, the furious King decided that Raleigh’s stay of execution decreed in 1603 should now come to an end. Sir Walter Raleigh was executed shortly afterwards.
text: 在众多传奇探险家与征服者之中，英国作家兼冒险家沃尔特·雷利爵士（约1554—1618）是最耀眼的人物之一。1580年，他镇压了反对英格兰占领的爱尔兰叛乱，由此崭露头角。<n><n>他成为伊丽莎白一世女王的宠臣，并利用自己的影响力筹资远征，寻找南美洲传说中的黄金城埃尔多拉多。数次远征都一无所获，但他凭借非凡的说服力，始终赢得伦敦出资人的支持。他让他们相信，最终的宝藏总在下一处河口后面，因此此刻绝不能放弃。<n><n>不过，他的信用最终还是耗尽了。人们一次次听到他豪迈的承诺，事后却发现全是空话。雷利终于失去了伊丽莎白的宠信。继位的詹姆斯一世认为，这个热血冒险家威胁到了自己较为温和的外交政策，因此一登基便以牵强的罪名将他逮捕并判处死刑。后来，死刑暂缓执行——请注意，并不是撤销！雷利被关进了伦敦塔。<n><n>多年后，国家财政状况迫使国王重新考虑，他批准沃尔特·雷利爵士率领另一支远征队前往圭亚那。这实在荒谬：一个自己尚负死刑的人，竟被授予掌握他人生死的权力，还奉命出海寻金！不过，这种矛盾很快就结束了。此时已饱受高烧折磨的雷利，亲眼见证了最后一次远征的失败。<n><n>他返回英格兰后，愤怒的国王决定结束自1603年起给予他的缓刑。不久，沃尔特·雷利爵士被处决。

source: The first encounters between the native inhabitants of the New World and the white seafarers generally passed off peacefully. In many places, the Europeans were greeted as gods. Here and there, this impression was based on old myths, but in most cases, the Native Americans were simply impressed by the tall blonde strangers that arrived in shimmering armor on their “water houses” (ships).<n><n>Columbus, Cortez and all the other explorers were only too delighted to perpetuate this illusion, but the Native Americans were confronted with the brutal reality soon enough: Driven by their insatiable lust for gold, the “Spanish disease” as the Native Americans called it, the Spaniards abused, enslaved and massacred entire populations. The sight of horses, hitherto unknown in America, and the sound of the canons caused utter panic and those that survived the massacre soon succumbed to smallpox, influenza or another imported disease.<n><n>Famous intellectuals such as Gonzolo Oviedo or Juan de Sepulveda tried to justify the crimes committed by the Europeans by using blood-curdling racist arguments that portrayed the native American race as being base, ignorant and inferior.<n><n>The same men who had scientists and witches burnt at the stake because of their beliefs, were well versed in the art of creating shocking accounts of the “bestial customs” of the Native Americans: Although the practices of idolatry, sacrificing humans and cannibalism were by no means imaginary, they were used henceforth by the white man as a blanket justification for imposing the most brutal sanctions of every kind on the Native Americans.
text: 新大陆原住民与白人航海者最初的接触，通常是和平的。在许多地方，欧洲人甚至被当作神灵迎接。有时，这种印象源于古老传说；但更多时候，原住民只是惊叹于那些身披闪亮铠甲、乘坐“水上房屋”（船只）而来的高大金发陌生人。<n><n>哥伦布、科尔特斯和其他探险者都乐于维持这种错觉，但原住民很快就面对了残酷的现实。在无尽的黄金欲望驱使下——原住民称之为“西班牙病”——西班牙人虐待、奴役乃至屠杀整个族群。美洲此前从未出现过的马匹和震耳欲聋的炮声引起了极度恐慌；即使逃过屠杀，幸存者也很快死于天花、流感或其他传入的疾病。<n><n>贡萨洛·奥维耶多、胡安·德·塞普尔韦达等知名学者，试图用令人毛骨悚然的种族主义论调，为欧洲人的罪行辩护，把美洲原住民描绘成卑劣、无知而低等的族群。<n><n>正是这些因信仰问题而将学者和所谓女巫送上火刑柱的人，最擅长编造骇人听闻的原住民“野蛮习俗”故事。偶像崇拜、人祭和食人行为虽并非凭空捏造，却从此被白人当成对原住民施加各种残酷惩罚的万能借口。

source: As is generally known, the early phase of the colonization of America was undertaken by Spain and Portugal. They were later joined by Holland and, most importantly, by England and France. What is rather less well known is that numerous Spanish expeditions would never have been undertaken had it not been for their powerful German financial backers.<n><n>By the year 1500, Upper Swabia and Augsburg in particular had developed into one of the most important centers of trade and finance in Europe. From here, the merchant families of Fugger and Welser exerted a powerful influence over world politics. For example, it was their extensive financial support that helped King Charles of Spain become Emperor of Germany in 1519. King Henry VIII of England and many of the Popes were happy to count Jakob Fugger the “Wealthy” among their friends.<n><n>Naturally, these astute traders had their own ulterior motives in bestowing this kind of support. In return, they expected to be assigned privileges or permission to participate in the royal mining of silver. The Welsers even managed to temporarily acquire part of the northern coast of Venezuela, where they founded towns such as “New Augsburg” and from where they sent several expeditions on (mostly fruitless) searches into the heartland for treasure.
text: 众所周知，美洲殖民最初由西班牙和葡萄牙主导，后来荷兰也加入其中，而英格兰和法国尤其重要。较少有人知道的是，若没有实力雄厚的德意志金融家的支持，许多西班牙远征根本不会成行。<n><n>到1500年，上施瓦本，尤其是奥格斯堡，已发展为欧洲最重要的贸易与金融中心之一。富格尔和韦尔瑟商人家族从这里对世界政治施加巨大影响。例如，正是他们的大量资助，帮助西班牙国王查理于1519年成为德意志皇帝。英格兰国王亨利八世和多位教皇，都乐于把“富豪”雅各布·富格尔视为朋友。<n><n>这些精明的商人提供支持，自然另有打算。他们期望以此换取特权，或获准参与王室的白银开采。韦尔瑟家族甚至一度取得委内瑞拉北部的一段海岸，在那里建立“新奥格斯堡”等城镇，并派出多次探险队深入内陆寻宝，但大多一无所获。

source: By conquering half of the globe, the Spanish Crown found itself able to avail of unique opportunities. Over a period of several centuries, up until the demise of the great American cultures of the Incas, Mayas and Aztecs and the discovery of huge silver deposits in Peru and Mexico by the latest, Spain’s position appeared to be unassailable. It seems almost absurd that it was precisely this immense wealth that precipitated this world power’s decline.<n><n>A large part of the treasures sent by ship back to Spain went directly into the pockets of those traders north of the Pyrenees who had financed the voyages in the first place. However, the remainder was still sufficient to drive up price levels on the Iberian peninsula. People there began living beyond their means: In an age where the ability to hold court on a grand scale was considered more important than balancing the state budget, people payed little attention to trivial financial concerns.<n><n>Goods were imported in ever increasing quantities aboard foreign ships because people had become far too refined to produce them at home. Even the equipment and provisions for the expeditions to America were seldom provided by the domestic traders. People remarked with pride: All of Europe is at Spain’s command.<n><n>However, the flow of silver had to run dry eventually, and the rude awakening that followed would resemble a hangover after a long night’s drunken carousing: The Dutch and the British were attempting to drive Spain from the high seas. Numerous religious wars against the protestant “heretics” and against the Turks had devoured enormous sums of money and the vast empire, on which the sun never set, had developed into an ungovernable colossus.<n><n> The crisis was apparent to all in the year 1557, when the new Spanish ruler, Philip II, was forced to declare state bankruptcy for the first time. The great empire, which had held greater treasures than any empire that had gone before, was broke.
text: 征服半个世界，为西班牙王室带来了独一无二的机遇。几个世纪以来，随着美洲印加、玛雅和阿兹特克文明的覆亡，以及秘鲁和墨西哥巨额银矿的发现，西班牙的地位似乎已不可撼动。然而，恰恰是这惊人的财富加速了这个世界强国的衰落，实在近乎荒诞。<n><n>运回西班牙的财宝，很大一部分直接流入比利牛斯山以北那些商人的口袋——最初正是他们出资支持远航。即便如此，余下的财富仍足以推高伊比利亚半岛的物价。人们开始入不敷出：在那个时代，宫廷的排场被看得比国家收支平衡更重要，谁还会在意这些琐碎的财政问题。<n><n>外国船只运来的进口商品越来越多，因为人们自认为过于高贵，不屑在本国生产。甚至远征美洲所需的装备和补给，也很少由本国商人提供。人们还自豪地宣称：整个欧洲都在听候西班牙差遣。<n><n>然而，白银之流终有枯竭之日。随后的猛醒，就像彻夜纵酒后的宿醉：荷兰和英国企图把西班牙赶出大洋；对新教“异端”和土耳其人的多次宗教战争吞噬了巨额资金；庞大的日不落帝国也成了难以统治的巨人。<n><n>1557年，危机终于暴露无遗：新国王腓力二世被迫首次宣布国家破产。这个拥有比以往任何帝国都更多财宝的大帝国，竟然没钱了。

source: Why is it that the language spoken in Brazil is Portuguese, when almost everywhere else in South America, it is Spanish?<n><n>Well, both the Spaniards and the Portuguese, who had discovered the sea route to India along the African coast, recognized early on that their future lay across the oceans. Each jealously watched the other to make sure that, in their hunt for goods, subjects and land, they did not encroach on each other’s territory.<n><n>As there was no such thing as international law at that time, in cases of conflict, they turned to the Pope, who was the only person to whose authority both nations were prepared to submit. For its part, the Catholic Church had an interest in ensuring that the Spaniards and Portuguese zealously pursued the Christianization of “heathens” in the unknown lands instead of wasting their energies making life difficult for one another.<n><n>Agreement was therefore reached during joint negotiations in Tordesillas (1494) and Saragossa (1529) that the newly discovered territories to the west of a particular line of longitude should belong to Spain and all others to Portugal. This line of longitude cut across what was at that time undiscovered South America so that its eastern side, part of what is now Brazil, fell to Portugal.
text: 为什么南美洲几乎处处都说西班牙语，巴西说的却是葡萄牙语？<n><n>西班牙人和沿非洲海岸发现通往印度海路的葡萄牙人，都很早就意识到，自己的未来在大洋彼岸。为了搜寻货物、臣民和土地，双方彼此警惕，唯恐对方侵入自己的势力范围。<n><n>当时还没有国际法，一旦发生冲突，他们便求助于教皇，因为只有他的权威能让两国都愿意服从。天主教会也希望西班牙人和葡萄牙人积极在未知土地上向“异教徒”传播基督教，而不是把精力浪费在相互刁难上。<n><n>于是，双方通过1494年在托尔德西里亚斯和1529年在萨拉戈萨的谈判达成协议：某条经线以西新发现的领土归西班牙，其余归葡萄牙。这条经线穿过当时尚未发现的南美洲，因此它东侧的土地，也就是今天巴西的一部分，落到了葡萄牙手中。

source: It was probably the Roman writer Polybius who first mentioned the word “pirate” (peirato) at around 140 BC. Since then, many different words have been used to refer to these fearful seafaring villains: Corsairs, freebooters, buccaneers, filibusters ... The men who surrounded Klaus Störtebeker were known as “The Vitalian Brotherhood” and Bartholomew Roberts gave himself and his band of murderous thugs the rather innocuous title “Gentlemen of Fortune”. Ultimately, however, it made little difference to the trader who it was who emerged out of the void to attack his ship. <n><n>Buccaneers have been a scourge to mankind down through the ages in every corner of the world. In ancient times, the Cicilian pirates spread such terror across the entire Mediterranean that the Roman Empire was forced to mount regular campaigns against them. Hidden islands and jagged coastlines located near to frequently-traveled trade routes provided the ideal locations for pirate activity: Those areas where reefs, currents and bad weather conditions made easy targets of the cumbersome trading ships provided a refuge to which one could quickly retreat after the outrage had been committed. The coast of Asia Minor was as feared in ancient times as the Caribbean was during the Age of Discovery, while the pirates of Southeast Asia assumed an almost mythical status.<n><n>According to the origins of the word, a “buccaneer” was actually a seaman who put to sea as a private individual, not as a sailor of the navy, in search of booty and who was therefore considered to be engaged in piracy. <n><n>However, the issuing of Letters of Marque gave some of the Caribbean buccaneers a semblance of legality. These documents were issued by English, French or Dutch governors and their purpose was to direct the scourge of piracy at the opposing powers.<n><n> The ease with which Letters of Marque could be obtained depended on the particular governor. One governor would consider it dishonorable to enter into a pact with pirates. Others were rather less scrupulous or may simply have been corrupt or cowardly.
text: 最早提到“海盗”（peirato）一词的人，可能是公元前140年左右的罗马作家波利比乌斯。此后，人们用过许多不同的称呼来指代这些令人畏惧的海上恶徒：海盗、私掠者、布坎海盗、劫掠者……克劳斯·施特尔特贝克的追随者被称为“粮食兄弟会”，而巴塞洛缪·罗伯茨则给自己和手下那群杀人不眨眼的暴徒取了个听来颇为温和的名字：“幸运绅士”。但对商人而言，从海面突然现身并攻击自己船只的究竟是哪一伙人，最终都没有多大区别。<n><n>自古以来，海盗就是世界各地人类社会的祸患。古代奇里乞亚海盗的恐怖活动遍及整个地中海，迫使罗马帝国定期出兵征讨。繁忙贸易航线附近的隐秘岛屿和曲折海岸，是海盗活动的理想场所：暗礁、洋流和恶劣天气让笨重的商船成为轻易得手的猎物，而海盗作恶之后又能迅速退入藏身之地。古代的小亚细亚海岸，与大航海时代的加勒比海一样令人畏惧；东南亚海盗的事迹更几乎成了传奇。<n><n>从词源来看，“私掠者”原本指以私人身份出海寻求战利品的水手，而非海军军人，因此其行为也被视为海盗活动。<n><n>不过，私掠许可证的签发，让部分加勒比私掠者获得了一层合法外衣。这些文件由英格兰、法国或荷兰总督签发，目的是把海盗之祸引向敌对势力。<n><n>私掠许可证是否容易取得，取决于具体的总督。有些人认为与海盗结盟有损荣誉，另一些人则不那么在意原则，或干脆就是腐败、怯懦之徒。

source: The “seven seas” are actually only three (namely, the three oceans): The North and South Pacific, the North and South Atlantic, the Arctic and Antarctic Oceans and the Indian Ocean.<n><n> The Pacific Ocean owes its name to the first circumnavigation of the globe by Fernando Magellan, who had the good fortune to encounter favorable weather during the many hungry weeks it took him to cross this vast ocean.<n><n>And another thing: The Caribbean derives its name from the “Karibe” (or “Karaibe”), the peoples of an Indian language group, whose area of settlement stretched from the Antilles along the northern coast of South America.
text: 所谓“七海”，其实只属于三个大洋：北太平洋与南太平洋、北大西洋与南大西洋、北冰洋与南冰洋，以及印度洋。<n><n>太平洋的名字源自费尔南多·麦哲伦的首次环球航行。在横越这片辽阔海洋的许多个饥肠辘辘的星期里，他幸运地遇上了平静的好天气。<n><n>还有一件事：加勒比海的名字来自“Karibe”或“Karaibe”，即属于同一个印第安语族的一些民族。他们的聚居地区从安的列斯群岛延伸到南美洲北部海岸。

source: The Bermuda Islands are named after the Spanish explorer Juan Bermúdez who discovered them in 1503. The infamous area known to all seafarers as the “Bermuda Triangle”, in which the risk of mysterious shipping accidents is said to be very high, covers an area of the sea between the Bermuda Islands, Puerto Rico and Fort Lauderdale (Florida).<n><n>Some people maintain that the strange series of inexplicable events started with the voyage of Christopher Columbus: The seafarer from Genoa in the service of Spain found himself with his three ships on September 14th 1492 in this very area, when his compass needle began to spin wildly. This was caused by the difference between the geographic north pole and the magnetic north pole. The next day, an enormous flame appeared in the sky (possibly a meteor).<n><n>However, the nickname “Bermuda Triangle” only emerged after the Second World War, following a series of aircraft accidents that drew the public’s attention to this area in the southwest of the North Atlantic.<n><n>Followers of mysterious events point to more than 200 alleged unexplained accidents, although they interpret the borders somewhat generously. Most of these events, a large number of which did not even occur in the area, have a perfectly logical explanation.
text: 百慕大群岛得名于1503年发现它们的西班牙探险家胡安·贝尔穆德斯。航海者们熟知的“百慕大三角”，指的是百慕大群岛、波多黎各与佛罗里达州劳德代尔堡之间的海域，据说那里神秘海难频发。<n><n>有人认为，这一连串无法解释的怪事始于哥伦布的航行：1492年9月14日，这位为西班牙效力的热那亚航海家率领三艘船经过这片海域时，罗盘指针突然疯狂转动。其原因在于地理北极与磁北极的位置不同。第二天，天空中又出现了一团巨大的火焰，可能是一颗流星。<n><n>不过，“百慕大三角”这一称呼直到第二次世界大战后才出现。当时，一系列飞机事故引起了公众对北大西洋西南部这片海域的关注。<n><n>神秘事件爱好者声称，这里发生过两百多起无法解释的事故，但他们对边界的划定相当宽松。其实，其中许多事件根本不发生在这片海域，而绝大多数都能得到完全合理的解释。

source: The legendary Spanish treasure fleet, which regularly set sail from America to Spain, also gave rise to all manner of greed beyond the Iberian peninsula. It was primarily an ambitious England who saw this as an opportunity to contest Spain’s role as mistress of the seas and queen of the world.<n><n>As the island kingdom was still too weak to engage in large-scale military campaigns, it made far more sense to engage its rival outside of Europe, far afield, where she would neither expect to be attacked nor receive any warning of attack. There, one could loot one’s victim with ease and then simply disappear and no one in Europe would hear of the events for months.<n><n>Daring captains, the most famous of whom was Francis Drake (1540-1596), were issued with Letters of Marque by Her Majesty Elizabeth I. These Letters of Marque resembled a kind of blank check and were a license to loot that elevated Drake and his associates above the level of regular buccaneers and conferred on them the status of private robber barons in the service of a higher authority. They made an excellent job of it. Nowhere were Iberian ships and garrisons safe.<n><n>In 1578, Francis Drake traversed the Straits of Magellan and set off like a whirlwind on the hunt for Spanish booty along the Pacific coast of America. No one had ever dared to do this before! On his return to Plymouth harbor in 1580, Drake had become the second captain after Magellan to sail around the world. <n><n>Meanwhile, King Philip of Spain was boiling with rage and waved the Treaty of Tordesillas, under which His Holiness the Pope had adamantly declared the western hemisphere to be within Spain’s sphere of influence in 1494. – But how could this sort of protest have any affect on this peculiar island nation of Protestant heretics, who completely rejected the authority of the Pope in Rome and who even refused to adopt the modern Gregorian calendar until 1753, purely because it had been developed on the orders of Pope Gregory in 1582?<n><n>Once more, it seemed that the matter could only be resolved by means of war. Philip’s Armada set sail for England in 1588, but under the command of Sir Francis Drake, who had by now been made a knight, and with the help of several timely storms, the English succeeded in destroying the Spanish fleet. For hundreds of years afterwards, no one would challenge Great Britain’s position as the leading sea power.
text: 传说中的西班牙宝船队定期从美洲驶回西班牙，也激起了伊比利亚半岛之外各方的贪欲。野心勃勃的英格兰尤其把它视作机会，试图挑战西班牙称霸海洋、君临世界的地位。<n><n>这个岛国当时还太弱，无法发动大规模军事行动。因此，更明智的办法是在欧洲之外、遥远的海域打击对手：那里的人既料不到攻击，也得不到预警。袭击者可以轻易抢走财物，再消失无踪，而欧洲要几个月后才会听到消息。<n><n>伊丽莎白一世女王向大胆的船长们发放私掠许可证，其中最著名的是弗朗西斯·德雷克（1540—1596）。这些许可证犹如空白支票，准许持有人劫掠，使德雷克及其同伴不再只是普通海盗，而成为奉更高权威之命行事的私人掠夺者。他们干得相当出色，伊比利亚的船只和驻军无处安宁。<n><n>1578年，弗朗西斯·德雷克穿过麦哲伦海峡，像旋风般沿美洲太平洋海岸搜掠西班牙财宝。此前从未有人敢这样做！1580年返回普利茅斯港时，德雷克已成为继麦哲伦之后完成环球航行的第二位船长。<n><n>与此同时，西班牙国王腓力怒不可遏，挥舞着《托尔德西里亚斯条约》：1494年，教皇曾在该条约中坚决宣布，西半球属于西班牙的势力范围。然而，这样的抗议又怎能影响那个古怪的新教岛国？他们根本不承认罗马教皇的权威，甚至仅仅因为新历法是在1582年奉教皇格里高利之命制定，就一直到1753年才肯采用先进的格里高利历。<n><n>看来，事情又只能诉诸战争。1588年，腓力的无敌舰队驶向英格兰。但在已获封爵士的弗朗西斯·德雷克指挥下，加上几场及时风暴的帮助，英格兰成功摧毁了西班牙舰队。此后数百年，再无人能够挑战英国的海上霸主地位。

source: Without doubt, the voyages of Christopher Columbus (1451-1506) to America ranked among the greatest adventures ever undertaken by mankind. Even a writer could hardly dare to imagine such a tale of dramatic events and strange coincidences.<n><n>Although the navigator from Genoa had managed to convince the royal couple Isabella and Ferdinand of Spain of his idea that there was a western sea route to India, he was certainly not able to rely on the assent of the crew on board. Indeed, most of the crew were pressed into service: As punishment for misdemeanors against the Crown, the town of Palos was forced to provide two ships with crews.<n><n>The news of Columbus’ plan provoked expressions of horror. The crew was firmly convinced that they were sailing under the command of a madman who could only bring destruction on himself and all who sailed with him.<n><n>However, Columbus’ greatest enemy was superstition: Every imaginable tale of horror appeared to have made its way on board and any strange or sinister events only reinforced the sailor’s fears: A volcano erupted as they sailed past Tenerife, then they saw columns of fire in the sky and even the compass needle appeared to be playing tricks on the crew. If the ships were becalmed, this was seen as a bad omen. On the other hand, if they made good progress, this meant that the wind always blew from east to west and that they would never be able to turn around.<n><n>On many occasions, a mutiny appeared to be inevitable. One night, the captain heard footsteps and muttering outside his cabin, and only when he started to pray in a loud voice did the assassins lose courage and sneak away.<n><n>The most serious crises always broke out when what was thought to be an island on the horizon turned out once again to be nothing more than an optical illusion. It was just such an occurrence on October 10th that brought matters to a head. With great difficulty, Columbus negotiated an ultimatum of three days, after which the crew wanted to turn around (preferably without their captain). However, fate had other intentions: They did in fact sight land within these thee days. None of those present could have dreamt that, instead of Asia, they had stumbled upon a completely new and unknown continent.<n><n>Japan and China still lay thousands of nautical miles away and only for the unbelievable good fortune that a foreign continent lay in its path, Columbus’ expedition would have been lost. The morale of the crew was immediately lifted. None of them could recall ever having harbored thoughts of mutiny ...
text: 毫无疑问，克里斯托弗·哥伦布（1451—1506）前往美洲的航行，是人类历史上最伟大的冒险之一。即使是作家，恐怕也不敢虚构出如此跌宕起伏、充满离奇巧合的故事。<n><n>这位热那亚航海家虽然说服了西班牙的伊莎贝拉女王和斐迪南国王，相信向西航行也能抵达印度，却无法指望船员们同样赞同他的计划。事实上，大多数船员都是被迫服役的：帕洛斯镇因冒犯王室而受罚，必须提供两艘船及其船员。<n><n>哥伦布的计划一经传开，便引发阵阵惊恐。船员坚信，指挥他们的是个疯子，只会把自己和所有同行者带向毁灭。<n><n>然而，哥伦布最大的敌人其实是迷信。似乎所有能想象到的恐怖传说都被带上了船，任何怪异或不祥的现象都会加深水手们的恐惧：船队驶过特内里费岛时火山喷发，随后他们又看见天空中出现火柱，连指南针似乎也在戏弄他们。海上无风、船只停滞，被视为凶兆；可若航行顺利，又意味着风始终从东吹向西，他们将永远无法返航。<n><n>好几次，叛乱似乎已不可避免。一天夜里，哥伦布听见舱外传来脚步和低语，直到他高声祈祷，那些刺客才失去勇气，悄悄退去。<n><n>最严重的危机，总发生在地平线上被误认作岛屿的东西再次被证实不过是幻象之时。10月10日又出现了这种情况，矛盾终于激化。哥伦布费尽口舌，才争取到最后三天；三天一过，船员就要返航，最好还不用带上他们的船长。然而命运另有安排：他们确实在这三天里看到了陆地。在场的人谁也想不到，他们遇见的并不是亚洲，而是一片全新、未知的大陆。<n><n>日本和中国仍在数千海里之外。若非幸运得难以置信，恰有一块陌生大陆横在途中，哥伦布的远征队早已葬身大海。船员们顿时士气高涨，似乎谁也不记得自己曾想过叛乱……

source: Christopher Columbus had indeed discovered a new land mass (or rather: rediscovered, for the Vikings had already set foot on American soil during the middle ages), but he mistakenly announced that he had discovered a sea route to India.<n><n>While preparing the second and third of his four voyages, the Genoan collaborated with Amerigo Vespucci from Florence. It was he who first suggested that these lands to the west actually belonged to a new and unknown continent. This spectacular realization reignited public interest and whenever anyone discussed these new territories, the name Vespucci was sure to be mentioned.<n><n>In contrast, Christopher Columbus’ star was in decline. In the meantime, he had even been sent home in chains after complaints by the Caribbean settlers, and his death as an embittered and sick man in 1506 did not attract the attention it deserved.
